finding: The merge is skipped on a bare existence test (`[ -f ... ]`), but nothing requires `--merge -o` to write `merged.ndjson` atomically. §3.5 pins temp+rename for the run state and §3.3.1 pins the `.part`-then-rename dance for role files precisely because a half-written artifact must never look complete; the merged file, which the existence guard now treats as complete-or-absent, gets neither. An attempt killed mid-merge (cap, SIGTERM, driver death — all first-class outcomes in §3.4) leaves a truncated `merged.ndjson`, and every later attempt skips the merge, so the round is recorded from a partial finding set and no rule in the spec ever regenerates it.

finding: The record kinds' brief_command sequences the merge and the record with `;`, not `&&`: `[ -f $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson ] || tp review --merge ... -o $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson; tp review <spec> --record $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson`. §8a.4 makes `--merge` exit 1 when an input has content lines and none parsed — exactly the dropped-role case the release exists to catch — but with `;` the record step runs anyway, against a merged file that is absent or holds only the roles that did parse. The round is then frozen undercounted, which is the failure §8a.4 was written to prevent, in the one path (unattended) that has no human reading stderr. The spec never says whether a non-zero merge must abort the record, so one implementer writes `;` as given and another writes a guarded conjunction.

finding: The SessionStart hook injects `tp resume --compact` into every unit, and §6.2 defends only the decision not to branch on the hook *matcher* — it never asks which unit kinds the payload feeds a decision for. finding: §6.3 says a re-run record unit "re-records from it rather than merging over it", where `it` is a `merged.ndjson` that by then carries the dispositions `review-resolve`/`audit-fix` wrote, and that "re-recording a round already recorded rewrites that round's entry rather than adding one". The spec never says whether `--record` counts a non-PASS row that carries a `fixed`/`wontfix`/`duplicate` disposition. The two readings differ in whether a re-recorded round can turn clean after the fact — an implementer who filters disposed rows lets a rewrite drop a round's finding count to zero, which is a convergence-arithmetic change Non-Goal 4 forbids, while one who counts every non-PASS row keeps the recorded round stable. Both are defensible from the text.
